hero.headline: DeSantis vetoes sovereign immunity bill that would have raised liability caps for government negligence
hero.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis vetoed legislation that would have increased damage caps in lawsuits against government entities for the first time in 16 years. The measure passed the Legislature with overwhelming bipartisan support in March but faced the governor's veto this week. The bill would have raised caps on damages payable in court settlements for people harmed by government negligence from $200,000 per person and $300,000 per incident to $350,000 per person and $500,000 per incident. The current caps were last set in 2010.

DeSantis said raising the caps would generate more unmeritorious lawsuits and undermine efforts to discourage frivolous claims. "When you raise the cap, you are going to generate more unmeritorious lawsuits," he said. The bill, sponsored by Sarasota Republican Representative Fiona McFarland with a companion measure from Lake Mary Republican Senator Jason Brodeur, drew opposition from more than 240 registered lobbyists representing counties, cities, and local agencies facing budget concerns. The measure would have allowed local governments to voluntarily settle claims exceeding the caps without seeking legislative approval. It was scheduled to take effect October 1 if signed.

Under Florida's sovereign immunity statutes, people harmed by government negligence must seek legislative passage of special claims bills to receive compensation above the damage caps. Lawmakers consider roughly a dozen such claims bills annually with varying success rates. This year, just over one-third of 14 claims bills passed both chambers, including cases involving a man paralyzed in a police van, a motorist injured in a crash with a state tractor, and a young girl harmed due to Department of Children and Families negligence despite prior warning signs. McFarland argued the current system creates unequal protection. "If you or I or one of our loved ones is hit by a truck, we have to pay attention to what's on the side of that truck," she said. "Depending on whether there's a corporate logo or a government seal, we have different access to monetary wholeness."

DeSantis countered that the current system works effectively. "I signed a number of claims bills this year," he said. "People have gotten millions of dollars with that." The Florida Justice Association criticized the veto, calling it a gift to insurance companies and a disservice to families seeking accountability for government negligence. The group noted that victims often wait years or more than a decade for compensation under the current system. It remains unclear whether McFarland or Brodeur will refile the legislation in 2027, when a new governor will hold veto power.

cards.headline: Driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
cards.body:
A 40-year-old man was killed early Sunday after a head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 2 a.m. near State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane.

FHP said a 2015 Kia Optima was traveling north on SR-710 when the driver crossed into the southbound lane and collided head-on with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The front left of the Kia struck the front left of the Tundra. Upon impact, the Kia burst into flames and came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra came to rest facing southeast in the southbound lane.

The driver of the Kia, a 40-year-old man, died at the scene. The driver of the Tundra, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, was transported via Lifestar from the scene.

FHP is investigating the crash. The Florida Highway Patrol continues to gather information about the circumstances that led to the collision on State Road 710.

cards.headline: FIFA clears U.S. striker Folarin Balogun to play Belgium in World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: The FIFA Disciplinary Committee confirmed that United States striker Folarin Balogun will be eligible to play against Belgium on Monday in Seattle after his one-match suspension was suspended.
cards.body:
The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has ruled that United States men's national team striker Folarin Balogun will be eligible to compete against Belgium in the Round of 16 match scheduled for Monday in Seattle. The 25-year-old forward had been facing an automatic one-match suspension after receiving a straight red card during the USMNT's 2-0 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina on July 1. Balogun was sent off in the 64th minute following a VAR review for a challenge where he stepped on the ankle of Bosnian defender Tarik Muharemovic, an offense classified as serious foul play.

FIFA invoked Article 27 of its disciplinary code to overturn the suspension. This provision allows the judicial body to fully or partially suspend the implementation of an on-pitch disciplinary measure and place it under a probationary period. According to FIFA's ruling, the match suspension remains suspended for a probationary period of one year. The red card will stay on Balogun's record, but his mandatory suspension has been put on hold. However, if he commits another similar infringement during the one-year period, the suspension will be immediately reinstated along with any additional penalties.

Balogun has been central to coach Mauricio Pochettino's attacking strategy throughout the tournament. The forward leads the USMNT in scoring with three goals in four matches before his dismissal against Bosnia and Herzegovina, where he scored during the first half before his exit. U.S. Soccer expressed its satisfaction with the FIFA decision in a statement released Sunday: "We accept the decision of the Disciplinary Committee and are pleased that Folarin Balogun is eligible to compete tomorrow. Our full attention is focused on the Round of 16 match against Belgium in Seattle, and we look forward to the continued support of our amazing fans."

This is not the first time FIFA has applied Article 27 to keep a star player available for crucial tournament matches. In November, Portuguese captain Cristiano Ronaldo faced a three-match ban for violent conduct after receiving a straight red card for an elbow against the Republic of Ireland in a qualifier. After serving one match against Armenia, FIFA commuted his remaining two-game suspension to a one-year probation period, citing his clean disciplinary history. That decision allowed Ronaldo to compete in Portugal's opening group matches. FIFA's decision to show similar leniency with Balogun demonstrates how the committee uses its discretionary authority to keep major tournament contenders at full strength during critical matches.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins' wife of running anonymous social media accounts
cards.teaser: Multiple anonymous social media accounts were deactivated after Governor Ron DeSantis' former communications staff publicly alleged the accounts were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins.
cards.body:
Christina Pushaw, a Communications Specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, accused Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, of operating anonymous social media accounts. Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador indicating that the account @FSUdude01670 was connected to a phone number and email similar to ones used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots of two-factor authentication messages showing an email address with letters starred out and a phone number displaying only the last digits. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, which she said also appeared tied to Layla Collins.

Pushaw stated the @bobnamy1 account's content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the Governor. Redfern confirmed the allegations, stating the FSUdude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern made their criticisms public. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year as Collins develops a statewide profile to run for Governor. Notably, both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretary for DeSantis. Redfern currently works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor.

cards.headline: Supreme Court allows states to count absentee ballots received after Election Day
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward, preserving grace period laws that election officials in several states depend on to process ballots.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court handed election administrators across the country significant clarity Monday, ruling 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward. The ruling centered on a Mississippi law allowing ballots received up to five business days after Election Day to count, provided they bear an Election Day postmark. A panel of three Trump-appointed 5th Circuit judges had struck the law down in 2024, reading federal election statutes to require ballots to be received, not merely cast, by Election Day. The Supreme Court reversed that ruling.

Justice Amy Coney Barrett, herself a Trump appointee, wrote the majority opinion and was joined by Chief Justice John Roberts and the three liberal Justices. Barrett wrote that federal law establishes when voters must make their choice, not when officials must have their ballots in hand. The ruling preserves grace period laws that election officials in roughly 30 states depend on to process ballots. Florida does not have a general postmark grace period, as state law requires mail ballots in hand by 7 p.m. on Election Day, so the ruling does not change existing practice here.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd asks court to keep Paula Stark off House District 47 ballot
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd filed court papers disputing St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark's account of a paperwork mix-up, with five state employees providing sworn declarations contradicting her claims.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd has asked a Leon Circuit Court to keep Republican Paula Stark off the House District 47 ballot, disputing her account of a paperwork mix-up. Stark's qualifying materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline on June 12, missing the required Form 6 disclosure of financial interests. Five state employees submitted sworn written declarations stating that Stark's Treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the Form 6 and was not accidentally handed it back when he submitted the rest of the paperwork. Election Records Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve said in a court declaration that three weeks after the qualifying deadline, Stark still had not submitted the Form 6. Byrd argued that had Stark or Davis questioned why the form was allegedly handed back, the mistake would have been discovered while Davis was at the Division.

Reeve detailed Stark's history of paperwork problems, including campaign finance reports filed over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. If Stark remains off the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 will open to all voters choosing between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. No other Republican filed to run in the traditionally blue seat covering parts of Osceola and Orange counties. Ballots are required to be mailed to overseas military members by July 4, with vote-by-mail ballots going out July 9-16.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year
hero.teaser: According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago.
hero.body:
The Fourth of July cookout tradition is getting pricier this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points squarely at inflation, with ground beef up 5.5% and buns up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%, while ice cream prices have risen 5.3%.

Not everything is more expensive, though. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said families can keep costs in check by shopping savvier than ever and comparing stores to see who has the best deals for groceries on their list. She emphasized that the biggest thing for families is cutting down food waste, which begins with a meal plan.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic to South Florida roads
cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million made the trip by car.
cards.body:
Friday's wet weather made for a tough start to the holiday weekend on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd said it's really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive. Despite the conditions, drivers pressed on.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. They find that where you're coming from, where you're going, and what time you leave can all impact your experience on the road. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and reported smooth sailing, saying they didn't see any traffic, no accidents or anything. Meanwhile, driver Fernando Amado described a very different experience, saying it's been pretty busy, especially with the weather.

For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday, and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive 'A' rating from state
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84 percent, received either an "A" or "B" rating, up from 120 schools the previous year. School grades are based on factors including student performance on state tests, graduation rates and performance in advanced coursework. District leaders reported that 86 percent of seniors participated in college-level coursework, completing at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education or Dual Enrollment course. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach experienced a significant turnaround, jumping from a "C" rating to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has led the school for 15 years after serving five years as assistant principal, said the improvement began when staff examined the foundations of student learning. The school modified its early childhood curriculum program, which serves students starting at age 3 and transitions into kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels. The school also fine-tuned its entire academic approach to challenge both students and staff to raise expectations across campus. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating this year, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary and West Gate Elementary.

hero.headline: Palm Beach County Fire Rescue responds to 29 fires during Fourth of July overnight
hero.teaser: Fire crews battled 29 fires across Palm Beach County during the overnight hours of the Fourth of July holiday.
hero.body: Palm Beach County Fire Rescue responded to 29 fires across the county during overnight hours on the Fourth of July holiday, with crews dispatched to the fires between 8 p.m. Saturday and 2 a.m. Sunday while residents celebrated Independence Day. Of the 29 fires, 11 were brush fires, 15 involved trash or dumpsters, 2 were structure fires, and one was miscellaneous. Fire rescue officials said firefighters quickly contained every fire with no major property damage reported. The department is reminding residents who continue to celebrate the holiday weekend to do so safely and responsibly.

hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating that every event hosted, project completed, and challenge overcome happens because the community shows up for one another.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road as widening project continues
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike. The move aims to accommodate growth in the city over the next 20 to 50 years.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city and the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

Erin Scheumeister, a Port St. Lucie resident, said the construction can be annoying but she believes it is necessary and will make it easier to get to work. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce's Peacock House Art Foundation offers tours, classes and artist residencies at historic Crain Estate
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination at the historic Crain Estate. The non-profit preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain while hosting international artists and offering classes for all skill levels.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation operates at the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce's Peacock Arts District, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain. Jaxson, a tile worker by trade, created all the tiling throughout the facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Art director Krystal Masters said the foundation keeps the property 90% the way it was when the Crains lived there and wants to avoid commercialization. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, bringing in seven originally that have now grown to over 100. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old, who walks with a limp and is hand-fed every day in his own bowls.

The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with Masters leading one-on-one classes designed for complete beginners. Masters, who does sculpting and watercolor work, said art is a form of therapy that destresses people and allows them to walk away fulfilled without scrolling on their phones.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem Blue Cross denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her breast reconstruction surgery denied by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. The insurer said the surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health." Clark said she expected her insurance company to support her recovery at that critical time.

GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh that has become a controversial treatment for breast reconstruction. While it is popular among plastic surgeons and approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined." Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week later after her surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington, found a mechanism to make it happen. Billington uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it gives her patients the least amount of complications. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Marine Unit rescues two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters were rescued Wednesday after their small motorized boat took on water and became submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway. Both occupants were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat until help arrived.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1, thanks to a quick response from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit and their decision to wear life jackets. The Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded, showing both occupants ending up in the water when their boat went down.

The boaters were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiancee Misty Dawn White in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home in Hobe Sound. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed their belongings.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé, Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said.

Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn described the situation as "completely a state of devastation." She reflected on White's character, saying, "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano. She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. The timing adds another layer of heartbreak, as Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July and she passed just a few days before it.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation, doubling slip capacity by July 2027
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long renovation project funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. The $3 million makeover is scheduled to be complete by July 4, 2027, and will nearly double the dock's slip capacity from 18 to 44 for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The project includes construction of a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. Mayor Sean Reed emphasized the safety benefits beyond capacity expansion. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it."

The closure has prompted the city to work with businesses depending on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates from the location, initially worried about continuing operations during construction. The city found a solution by allowing the company to build a gate at the non-floating section of the dock to board passengers. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the dock is central to Stuart's identity and economy. "Stuart is not Stuart without the water," he said. Boat captain Parker Fisher, based in Stuart, supports the renovation. "It's definitely needed some work over the years, so I'm glad they're putting money into it," Fisher said.

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde scare 3-2 to advance to World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday to advance to the World Cup Round of 16 after the island nation challenged the defending champion until the final minutes of extra time.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi and Argentina advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 with a 3-2 victory over Cape Verde on Friday in a thrilling match that extended into extra time. Messi scored in the 29th minute for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal. Lisandro Martinez added a goal in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1. Cape Verde's Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte both scored equalizers that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida. The go-ahead score for Argentina was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute.

Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday in the Round of 16. Egypt advanced by beating Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday. Cape Verde's goalkeeper Vozinha, 40 years old, made 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Cape Verde became the smallest country to reach the knockout round after securing draws against Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia in their memorable World Cup debut. Messi has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race, and extended his World Cup record to 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak.

cards.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with Venus due to knee injury
cards.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
cards.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. The 44-year-old lost her singles match 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 to 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. In an Instagram post, Serena said she was heartbroken to withdraw, stating that coming back to compete had been a gift and that the opportunity to play alongside Venus meant the world to her. "I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn't ready to compete," she wrote.

Serena's post included images of four syringes showing fluid drained from her knee after her singles match, along with a video of her walking with strapping on her right leg while one of her daughters held a cane for her. The Williams sisters, with Venus now 46, were scheduled to face Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in a first-round doubles match that had been pushed back to allow Serena more recovery time. The pair are six-time Wimbledon women's doubles champions together. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could compete elsewhere soon, telling fans to "stay tuned to a city near you." Venus competed in mixed doubles on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is working toward a state title run as they prepare for the 2026 fall season.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are setting their sights on a state title as they prepare for the 2026 fall football season. The team finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit left them feeling more was within reach. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year seniors who came from the middle school program. "They know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said. With this veteran senior class leading the way, the program is adopting a more demanding schedule this fall.

Senior Jack Williams said the team wanted to take the program to the next level by scheduling challenging games against strong teams to compete and attract new players. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that improvement is measured by postseason success, stating that going undefeated in the regular season does not matter if the team keeps losing in the second round of the playoffs. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts add up as something to look forward to, with the team working harder to see positive results when the season begins and break their record.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting season programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering a variety of educational programs during peak sea turtle nesting season this summer through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, these seasonal experiences are designed to help visitors learn about sea turtle conservation at one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe nesting turtles while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks at country club
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse hosted a full day of family activities, live entertainment and fireworks on July 4.
cards.body:
North Palm Beach residents and visitors celebrated Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The free community event included a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. The festivities began with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests enjoyed a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar.

Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families took part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign began around 6 p.m. Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course offered one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse hosted a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: DeSantis vetoes sovereign immunity bill that would have raised liability caps for government negligence
hero.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis vetoed legislation that would have increased damage caps in lawsuits against government entities for the first time in 16 years. The measure passed the Legislature with overwhelming bipartisan support in March but faced the governor's veto this week. The bill would have raised caps on damages payable in court settlements for people harmed by government negligence from $200,000 per person and $300,000 per incident to $350,000 per person and $500,000 per incident. The current caps were last set in 2010.

DeSantis said raising the caps would generate more unmeritorious lawsuits and undermine efforts to discourage frivolous claims. "When you raise the cap, you are going to generate more unmeritorious lawsuits," he said. The bill, sponsored by Sarasota Republican Representative Fiona McFarland with a companion measure from Lake Mary Republican Senator Jason Brodeur, drew opposition from more than 240 registered lobbyists representing counties, cities, and local agencies facing budget concerns. The measure would have allowed local governments to voluntarily settle claims exceeding the caps without seeking legislative approval. It was scheduled to take effect October 1 if signed.

Under Florida's sovereign immunity statutes, people harmed by government negligence must seek legislative passage of special claims bills to receive compensation above the damage caps. Lawmakers consider roughly a dozen such claims bills annually with varying success rates. This year, just over one-third of 14 claims bills passed both chambers, including cases involving a man paralyzed in a police van, a motorist injured in a crash with a state tractor, and a young girl harmed due to Department of Children and Families negligence despite prior warning signs. McFarland argued the current system creates unequal protection. "If you or I or one of our loved ones is hit by a truck, we have to pay attention to what's on the side of that truck," she said. "Depending on whether there's a corporate logo or a government seal, we have different access to monetary wholeness."

DeSantis countered that the current system works effectively. "I signed a number of claims bills this year," he said. "People have gotten millions of dollars with that." The Florida Justice Association criticized the veto, calling it a gift to insurance companies and a disservice to families seeking accountability for government negligence. The group noted that victims often wait years or more than a decade for compensation under the current system. It remains unclear whether McFarland or Brodeur will refile the legislation in 2027, when a new governor will hold veto power.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins' wife of running anonymous social media accounts
cards.teaser: Multiple anonymous social media accounts were deactivated after Governor Ron DeSantis' former communications staff publicly alleged the accounts were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins.
cards.body:
Christina Pushaw, a Communications Specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, accused Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, of operating anonymous social media accounts. Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador indicating that the account @FSUdude01670 was connected to a phone number and email similar to ones used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots of two-factor authentication messages showing an email address with letters starred out and a phone number displaying only the last digits. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, which she said also appeared tied to Layla Collins.

Pushaw stated the @bobnamy1 account's content consisted entirely of promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the Governor. Redfern confirmed the allegations, stating the FSUdude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern made their criticisms public. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year as Collins develops a statewide profile to run for Governor. Notably, both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretary for DeSantis. Redfern currently works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor.

cards.headline: Florida communities receive $7.2 million in FEMA grants for Hurricane Ian recovery projects
cards.teaser: Four Florida municipalities received new federal funding for infrastructure projects tied to Hurricane Ian recovery, four years after the Category 4 storm struck the state in September 2022.
cards.body:
FloridaCommerce announced $7.2 million in grants through the Hurricane Ian Hazard Mitigation Grant Match Program as part of FEMA local match requirements for infrastructure repairs and recovery. The funds are designed to provide infrastructure recovery, improve emergency preparedness and reduce the impact of future storms. Charlotte County will receive $5.83 million for a public works hurricane-safe room generator and $93,392 for a leachate waste plant generator project. The Port of the Islands Community Improvement District will receive $750,840 for a Union Road water storage and infrastructure retrofit project.

Seminole County has $319,437 earmarked for a mitigation reconstruction project on Shad Lane, while the city of Palatka will receive $283,996 for a lift station generator. Secretary of Commerce J. Alex Kelly stated that Florida communities are getting the support they need to bolster critical infrastructure and storm-readiness. Hurricane Ian made landfall near Fort Myers on September 22, 2022, as a Category 4 storm and plowed through the peninsula. The Ian HMGMP program has already distributed more than $12 million in grants to municipalities. FEMA funding is provided on the condition that local governments will match the same amount of local money to complete the projects.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd asks court to keep Paula Stark off House District 47 ballot
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd filed court papers disputing St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark's account of a paperwork mix-up, with five state employees providing sworn declarations contradicting her claims.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd has asked a Leon Circuit Court to keep Republican Paula Stark off the House District 47 ballot, disputing her account of a paperwork mix-up. Stark's qualifying materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline on June 12, missing the required Form 6 disclosure of financial interests. Five state employees submitted sworn written declarations stating that Stark's Treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the Form 6 and was not accidentally handed it back when he submitted the rest of the paperwork. Election Records Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve said in a court declaration that three weeks after the qualifying deadline, Stark still had not submitted the Form 6. Byrd argued that had Stark or Davis questioned why the form was allegedly handed back, the mistake would have been discovered while Davis was at the Division.

Reeve detailed Stark's history of paperwork problems, including campaign finance reports filed over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. If Stark remains off the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 will open to all voters choosing between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. No other Republican filed to run in the traditionally blue seat covering parts of Osceola and Orange counties. Ballots are required to be mailed to overseas military members by July 4, with vote-by-mail ballots going out July 9-16.

cards.headline: Supreme Court allows states to count absentee ballots received after Election Day
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward, preserving grace period laws that election officials in several states depend on to process ballots.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court handed election administrators across the country significant clarity Monday, ruling 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward. The ruling centered on a Mississippi law allowing ballots received up to five business days after Election Day to count, provided they bear an Election Day postmark. A panel of three Trump-appointed 5th Circuit judges had struck the law down in 2024, reading federal election statutes to require ballots to be received, not merely cast, by Election Day. The Supreme Court reversed that ruling.

Justice Amy Coney Barrett, herself a Trump appointee, wrote the majority opinion and was joined by Chief Justice John Roberts and the three liberal Justices. Barrett wrote that federal law establishes when voters must make their choice, not when officials must have their ballots in hand. The ruling preserves grace period laws that election officials in roughly 30 states depend on to process ballots. Florida does not have a general postmark grace period, as state law requires mail ballots in hand by 7 p.m. on Election Day, so the ruling does not change existing practice here.

cards.headline: United States men's soccer team faces Belgium in World Cup knockout round Monday
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle after earning the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team will face Belgium in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle on Monday night. The Americans earned their first knockout stage victory since 2002 after dispatching Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday, though they played the final 26 minutes plus stoppage time with 10 men following Folarin Balogun's red card. Longtime referee Andy Davies later told ESPN the decision was wrong, saying the contact was purely accidental and resulted from two players challenging for possession in a normal football movement. Coach Mauricio Pochettino said flatly it was never a red card, and the American camp noted that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament without receiving a card. Weston McKennie spoke for the locker room, calling the decision "a bit bogus."

Balogun, one of the team's top players, will watch from the stands as the Americans face Belgium, which earned a Round of 16 win over the U.S. in the 2014 World Cup. Belgium has won six consecutive meetings against the United States, including a 5-2 friendly rout in March, since the inaugural 1930 World Cup marked the lone American victory in the head-to-head series. The team is well-coached and physically capable, playing at a venue where the home crowd will be as loud as any in the tournament.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce historic estate into arts destination with global artist residency program
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is establishing Fort Pierce as an artistic hub by operating from the historic Crain Estate, a property that honors the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain. The non-profit preserves the home where the couple once lived, showcasing Mr. Crain's exceptional tile work that spans across floors, walls, and ceilings throughout the facility. According to Krystal Masters, the art director, the estate has remained largely unchanged since the Crains' era. Guided tours are available every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, allowing visitors to explore the lush gardens, vibrant architecture, and distinctive furnishings collected during the couple's nine trips around the world. One notable piece is a gazebo shipped from India, which features small peacock designs etched into its structure. The foundation has deliberately chosen to preserve the property's original character rather than commercialize it, maintaining details like the smoking and bourbon room with its distinctive wood paneling and stained glass.

The estate's name derives from over 100 peacocks that roam the grounds. The Crains are believed to have introduced these birds to Fort Pierce during the 1970s, starting with seven birds that have since multiplied significantly. Bob, a 60-year-old peacock with a distinctive limp, has become something of a celebrity on the property. He receives daily hand-feedings from staff and has his own designated bowls. Tour guides highlight how peacocks create memorable moments for young visitors, particularly when children feed the birds directly from their hands. The estate also has a colorful history with other animals. According to stories shared at the foundation, Jaxson Crain once traveled to South America, obtained a baby monkey, placed it in his pocket, and brought it back to the property.

The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program that welcomes creative professionals from across the globe. Participants stay in simple yet elegant accommodations on the estate grounds. Masters emphasizes that the program does not require prior professional experience, making it accessible to artists at various skill levels. The on-site art lab offers classes for both children and adults, with Masters teaching one-on-one sessions designed for beginners. Students with no prior experience can complete finished pieces during these classes, working with mediums including sculpting and watercolor. Recent workshops have featured projects like painting pets in watercolor.

For Masters, art extends beyond creative expression. "Art is a form of therapy and it distresses people," she explains. She finds fulfillment in seeing students leave the classes feeling happy and fulfilled, having engaged in meaningful creative work rather than scrolling through phones. The foundation's approach combines cultural preservation with community engagement, creating a space where artistic exploration thrives within a historically significant setting that celebrates the Crains' adventurous legacy.
